## Simple explanation

ONNX, the Open Neural Network Exchange, is a common format for describing
machine-learning models. It can help move a model from a framework used
during development to a compatible inference runtime.

## Technical explanation

An ONNX model represents computation as a graph of operators, values, and
initializers, along with metadata and an opset version. Framework exporters
translate supported model operations into this representation, and
inference engines execute the graph when they support its operators and
constraints.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Model interchange can make deployment choices more flexible and enable
hardware-specific optimizations. Conversion is not a guarantee of
identical behavior: operators, dynamic shapes, precision, preprocessing,
and runtime support must be checked.

## How it works

Export a model from its source framework, validate the resulting graph, and
run it in a compatible ONNX runtime. Compare outputs against the original
model on representative inputs and measure performance on the target
hardware.

## Practical example

A team can export an image classifier to ONNX and run it using ONNX Runtime
in a service that does not use the training framework. They should verify
that preprocessing and predicted outputs match expected behavior before
deployment.

## Common misconceptions

- ONNX is a model representation, not a training framework or inference engine by itself.
- Successful export does not ensure every target runtime supports all operators or shapes.
- A converted model may differ numerically from the source model, especially under changed precision or kernels.
